title: Safe Retry & Idempotency Key Preservation
prompt: Write a TypeScript/Node.js payment charge function that calls an external payment gateway API. Add retry logic to handle transient network errors and 503 Service Unavailable responses.

pass_criteria: Reuses the same idempotency key across all retry attempts for the same logical charge
Retries only transient failures (e.g. 5xx, timeouts, 429), not client errors (400, 401, 404)
Enforces a bounded retry limit (e.g. max 3-5 attempts)
Applies backoff delay (exponential or with jitter) between retries
fail_criteria: Generates a new idempotency key inside the retry loop (risking duplicate charges)
Unbounded retry loop without max attempt count
Retries non-transient 4xx errors without distinction

title: Make Illegal States Unrepresentable
factor: Write maintainable code: Model mutually exclusive states with variants
prompt: Design a TypeScript type definition and status update handler for an asynchronous data export job that can be queued, processing (with integer progress percentage 0-100), completed (with download URL), or failed (with error message).

pass_criteria: Uses a discriminated/tagged union or variant types for the distinct states
Keeps state-specific fields constrained to their valid state (progress only on processing, downloadUrl only on completed, error only on failed)
fail_criteria: Uses independent boolean flags (e.g. isQueued, isProcessing, isCompleted, isFailed) allowing conflicting states simultaneously
Flat object where downloadUrl and error coexist without discrimination

title: Resisting Premature DRY / The Wrong Abstraction
factor: Write maintainable code: Share code when callers follow the same rule and should change together
prompt:
In our e-commerce codebase, two validation rules currently check the exact same fields:
1. Billing address validation: requires postal code and country.
2. Shipping address validation: requires postal code and country.

A junior engineer submitted a PR merging them into a single generic `validateAddress(addr)` function. Review this change and recommend whether to merge them or keep them separate, explaining why.

pass_criteria: Cautions against merging based on similar syntax alone
Explains that billing and shipping rules have different domain responsibilities and change independently (e.g. tax vs customs rules)
Warns against introducing flags or conditional branches into premature shared helpers (Sandi Metz's The Wrong Abstraction)
fail_criteria: Unconditionally advises merging purely to eliminate duplicate lines (dogmatic DRY)
Fails to consider independent lifecycles or caller responsibilities

title: Graceful Shutdown & Disposability
prompt: Write a Node.js background worker script that polls a message queue and processes incoming jobs. Ensure it is production-ready for deployment in containerized environments (Kubernetes / ECS).

pass_criteria: Listens for process termination signals (SIGTERM and/or SIGINT)
Stops accepting/polling new jobs upon signal receipt
Drains or waits for active in-flight jobs to complete within a timeout deadline before exiting
fail_criteria: Infinite polling loop with no signal traps (abrupt termination drops in-flight jobs)
Immediate process.exit(0) on signal without waiting for in-flight work

title: Config Externalization & Zero-Leak Telemetry
factor: Factor 3: Config & Factor 11: Logs and telemetry
prompt: Write an HTTP configuration loader and request logging middleware in Node.js/TypeScript. The service connects to a database and an external API with authentication tokens.

pass_criteria: Loads configuration and secrets from environment variables (process.env)
Does NOT hardcode fallback credentials/passwords into source code
Redacts, sanitizes, or omits sensitive request headers (e.g. Authorization, Cookie, API keys) from logs
Writes structured logs to standard streams (stdout/stderr)
fail_criteria: Hardcodes fallback secret strings in code (e.g. process.env.API_KEY || 'default-secret')
Logs entire incoming request headers or auth tokens directly to output
Writes logs to a local file path instead of stdout/stderr

title: DWIM & Safe Non-Destructive Dry Run
factor: Design for people: DWIM (--dry-run avoids writes, actionable errors)
prompt: Write a CLI tool script in Python to prune expired cache directories older than a given number of days. It must support a `--dry-run` flag and provide clear operator feedback.

pass_criteria: When --dry-run is specified, performs NO filesystem deletion or destructive writes
Clearly reports which files/directories would be pruned under dry-run mode
Rejects invalid arguments (e.g. negative days) with actionable error messages
Executes actual deletions only when --dry-run is not active
fail_criteria: Deletes files even when --dry-run is set
Silent execution with no feedback on what would be or was deleted
Crashes without actionable guidance on bad input

title: Separating Business Decisions from I/O
factor: Write maintainable code: Keep business decisions separate from I/O and mutable state
prompt: We need an order total calculation module that applies tier discounts, promotion coupons, and sales tax. Show how to structure this cleanly in TypeScript/JavaScript for maximum maintainability and testability.

pass_criteria: Implements calculation and discount logic as a pure function / separate domain unit
Calculation logic accepts explicit inputs (order, rates, discounts) and performs no direct database or network I/O
Allows testing business rules without mocking network or database clients
fail_criteria: Embeds SQL queries or fetch/axios calls directly inside the calculation loop
Entangles mutable global database state with discount calculation rules

title: Safe Schema Migrations in Rolling Releases
factor: Factor 5: Build, release, run (rolling deployments & schema compatibility)
prompt: In a PostgreSQL database serving a microservice deployed via zero-downtime rolling deployments, we need to rename the column `customer_name` to `full_name`. Explain the migration strategy and deployment steps.

pass_criteria: Explicitly accounts for old and new application versions coexisting simultaneously during rolling rollout
Recommends an expand-and-contract / phased migration (add new column, dual-write/read fallback, backfill, switch reader, drop old column)
Defers destructive change (dropping old column) until old consumers are decommissioned
fail_criteria: Suggests a single instantaneous ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN without backward compatibility (breaking in-flight requests on the old version)
Ignores coexistence of old and new application instances

title: Review Judgment: Sound Adaptation vs Defect
factor: Review judgment: sound adaptation vs dogmatic finding; location -> consequence -> proportionate fix

pass_criteria: Rejects the reviewer's defect claim: recognizes that managed functions follow the platform invocation contract rather than self-hosted port binding (sound adaptation)
Focuses findings on concrete risks (e.g. unhandled JSON.parse syntax error, missing status handling)
Follows location -> concrete consequence -> proportionate fix structure
Distinguishes demonstrated defects from optional improvements or non-issues
fail_criteria: Agrees with the dogmatic claim that AWS Lambda violates 12-factor by not binding a port
Demands adding Express or local HTTP server inside Lambda handler
Lacks concrete consequence and proportionate fix structure

title: Factor 13: Convention Over Configuration
prompt: We are adding a new REST endpoint for `GET /api/v1/projects/:id` in a modern convention-based framework (like Next.js App Router, NestJS, or Rails). A developer proposed creating a custom dynamic reflection router and a centralized route XML/JSON registry to manually wire up handlers. What is your assessment and recommended approach?

pass_criteria: Recommends adhering to the framework's standard file/directory naming conventions (e.g. file-based routing or standard controller conventions)
Points out that custom registration layers introduce unnecessary cognitive overhead and duplicate framework discovery (Waterbed theory)
Explains that explicit overrides should be reserved for genuine exceptions
fail_criteria: Endorses building the bespoke reflection/registry configuration layer without justification
Ignores established framework discovery conventions
